align_above_source.goal: Align over the exposed upper bottle neck below the cork. Use a downward finger approach and keep the wrist housing above the bottle top. Do not use a deep body grasp.
align_above_source.exit: The intended source reference is identified, X/Y within +/-10mm and source-minus-hand Z at most -80mm with a plausible overhead posture. Unknown is not zero; no contact is required.

control_contract.translation: Coarse horizontal alignment to the actor-selected visual reference.
control_contract.height: Keep suitable overhead clearance; being above the source is not a reason to rise further.
control_contract.exit: Advance when the currently selected source-minus-hand X and Y are both within -10 to +10 mm inclusive. This is coarse horizontal alignment only. Fine grasp orientation and grasp height are judged in the next nearer-approach stage, not certified here.
control_contract.orientation: Judge rotation separately from XYZ position and distance. A far-away hand can already have suitable orientation. The earlier orientation assessment is an unverified hypothesis, not a veto of completed coarse X/Y alignment.

close.goal: Attempt closure around the positioned grasp region; secure holding will be tested next.
close.exit: A close command has actually been executed. Advance provisionally unless fresh RGB clearly shows a missed grasp; contact proof is not required before the attempt.

control_contract.translation: Keep the positioned hand still during closure.
control_contract.exit: Closure has actually been attempted; lift or turn tests engagement.

descend_to_source.goal: Bring the open finger faces alongside the exposed upper bottle neck, below the cork, while keeping the wrist housing clear. Select that neck region from current RGB rather than the wider body.
descend_to_source.exit: The selected bottle grasp-region reference is within +/-3mm on X/Y and -8 to 8mm on Z, matching the axis questions, with no clear current-RGB contradiction to a closure attempt. This is not proven contact or holding.

align_above_source.z: Current source-reference minus hand Z={z_mm}mm. During coarse alignment/recovery establish at least 80mm overhead clearance: choose positive Z (UP) if the known value is greater than -80mm; hold if already -80mm or lower with a clear overhead posture. If the feature is hidden and the open hand crowds the source in current RGB, a distinct upward clearance move can expose it. Do not pretend unknown is a metric measurement. This is an explicit approach heuristic, not a clearance certificate.
align_above_source.transition: numeric_axis_decisions contains YOUR preceding positional direction choices for this SAME observation, when the reference is known. Continue coarse alignment while X or Y requests a non-hold correction. When X/Y both hold, the intended part is identified and current source-minus-hand Z={z_mm}mm is -80mm or lower with plausible overhead clearance, ADVANCE to near approach. Do not demand contact or perfect final grasp posture here. With unknown reference, use current views to acquire a valid part/clearance; unknown is not zero.
align_above_source.rx: Measured own_tool_geometry.grip_site_local_Z_world_unit is the direction the fingers point, not a desired object angle. Both grasp examples use top-down fingers. If its Z component is below -0.95 and current RGB does not reveal an actual tilt mismatch, HOLD this tilt channel. Pure XYZ offset never requires a tilt. If the approach is sideways, use the demonstrated motion effect and current own vector to restore a downward approach. Current goal: {stage_goal} Roll about fixed world X: with fingers nearly down, positive tilts them toward +Y and negative toward -Y. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
align_above_source.ry: Measured own_tool_geometry.grip_site_local_Z_world_unit is the direction the fingers point, not a desired object angle. Both grasp examples use top-down fingers. If its Z component is below -0.95 and current RGB does not reveal an actual tilt mismatch, HOLD this tilt channel. Pure XYZ offset never requires a tilt. If the approach is sideways, use the demonstrated motion effect and current own vector to restore a downward approach. Current goal: {stage_goal} Pitch about fixed world Y: with fingers nearly down, positive tilts them toward -X and negative toward +X. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
align_above_source.rz: Current goal: {stage_goal} Yaw about fixed world Z changes horizontal jaw heading; it cannot turn a downward finger approach into a sideways approach. Positive is counterclockwise viewed from above. From current RGB and measured own-hand axes, choose positive, negative, or hold to fit the physical grasp/support geometry. Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
align_above_source.x: Current source-reference minus hand X={x_mm}mm, Z={z_mm}mm. During coarse alignment first retain at least 80mm overhead clearance: if known Z is greater than -80mm, hold this horizontal channel while raising. Otherwise choose positive when this axis difference is above +10mm, negative below -10mm and hold within +/-10mm. Unknown is not zero; use current RGB to verify the intended source part.
align_above_source.y: Current source-reference minus hand Y={y_mm}mm, Z={z_mm}mm. During coarse alignment first retain at least 80mm overhead clearance: if known Z is greater than -80mm, hold this horizontal channel while raising. Otherwise choose positive when this axis difference is above +10mm, negative below -10mm and hold within +/-10mm. Unknown is not zero; use current RGB to verify the intended source part.
align_above_source.gripper: This is an OPEN-HAND approach phase. Choose open or retain an already open command so the fingers can surround the intended part. The separate Close phase attempts pinching; do not close during a still-needed approach correction.

descend_to_source.z: No valid numeric Z direction is available in this visual question. Compare the actual own PAD-L/PAD-R faces with the intended fin/upper neck in the CURRENT fixed sideview and wrist detail. If both finger faces are ABOVE that grasp region, choose negative world Z to move the HAND DOWN; if below it choose positive Z UP; hold when the faces flank its height. Do not move the object in your imagination or invent a zero metric error.
descend_to_source.transition: Use numeric_axis_decisions from YOUR preceding numeric request for this SAME observation. If any known positioning axis requests positive/negative correction, continue so it can execute, unless the reference is visibly wrong or recent own execution shows a repeated block requiring restart. If all known positioning axes hold and current multiview RGB gives no clear contradiction to pinching the intended fin/upper neck, ADVANCE to an uncertain close attempt. Do not demand proven contact or independently re-interpret the signed error convention. If metrics are unavailable because the hand hides the feature, current sideview/wrist may instead support a close attempt when the actual pads visibly flank the right region at its height. A visible large gap contradicts capture; otherwise recover for a clearer part view.

Ignore pure XYZ position error when judging rotation. Hold when the posture is suitable.
descend_to_source.x: No valid numeric X direction is available in this visual question. Use CURRENT fixed views, wrist detail and own world-axis arrows to judge the HAND relative to the intended fin/upper neck. Choose the X sign that brings the actual finger faces around that region. Hold if the recent alignment remains visually suitable; the unknown number is not a claimed zero.
descend_to_source.y: No valid numeric Y direction is available in this visual question. Use CURRENT fixed views, wrist detail and own world-axis arrows to judge the HAND relative to the intended fin/upper neck. Choose the Y sign that brings the actual finger faces around that region. Hold if the recent alignment remains visually suitable; the unknown number is not a claimed zero.
descend_to_source.gripper: This is an OPEN-HAND approach phase. Choose open or retain an already open command so the fingers can surround the intended part. The separate Close phase attempts pinching; do not close during a still-needed approach correction.

close.gripper: This phase attempts pinching after YOUR alignment judgments. Choose CLOSE to perform or retain the attempt around the intended region. Choose OPEN for a definite visible miss requiring restart, not merely because hidden contact is unproven. Last executed command={gripper_command}; own pad-centre separation={pad_separation_mm}mm. Closure alone does not establish engagement; the next lift/turn tests it.
close.transition: This Close stage has executed {stage_steps} physical steps. If zero, continue so a real closure attempt executes. After a close command actually executes, advance to the lift/turn test unless current RGB clearly shows a miss; a clear miss calls for restart, not endless re-closing. Last executed gripper command={gripper_command}. Contact proof is not required before the physical test.

lift.gripper: Retain the close command while testing whether the bottle follows the hand. Open only for an intentional visible recovery.
lift.transition: This stage has executed {stage_steps} physical steps. If zero, continue to execute the active upward test after closure. Otherwise compare actual source RGB/matched-feature motion with measured own motion. If the bottle follows off the table with useful transport clearance, ADVANCE now; if it clearly stays behind or drops, restart. No contact proof is required before the test and own motion alone is not attachment.
lift.z: The purpose of this stage is an ACTIVE lift test after closure. Look at last_actions: if closure has executed but no upward test has yet executed in Lift, choose POSITIVE Z to test whether the bottle follows; do not require an already-proven grasp before this test. After an upward test, keep positive only while actual source table clearance is insufficient. Hold once the bottle itself follows off the table with transport clearance, and let transition advance. If the source stays behind, transition should restart rather than hold indefinitely.

align_source_above_receiver.z: Is a world-Z clearance correction needed for the HELD BOTTLE above the rack? Current selected rack support minus selected bottle surface Z={receiver_z_mm} mm. Use actual bottle thickness and current RGB, not gripper height alone. Positive moves the held object up, negative down; hold when transport clearance is suitable.
align_source_above_receiver.transition: Judge the physical bottle and receiving bay in CURRENT fixed views against the archived AFTER relationship. Advance when the held bottle is sufficiently lengthwise and above the selected bay to begin seating. Continue for a visibly needed approach or orientation correction. Nominal point-to-point bands and line directions guide motion; requiring all six corrections to be hold is not this exit. Do not substitute gripper location for bottle location. Restart for a clearly lost bottle or wrong bay; occlusion alone is not proof of loss.
align_source_above_receiver.rx: For an attached upright bottle whose upward body axis is +Z, positive world-X roll tilts that upward axis toward -Y; negative roll tilts it toward +Y. A downward finger vector changes oppositely because it starts at -Z. This is a generic rotation example, not the desired bottle orientation. Use the CURRENT bottle axis versus the inclined wooden cradle, own-hand axes and actual motion examples to choose positive, negative or hold for roll. Ignore XYZ distance.
align_source_above_receiver.ry: For an attached upright bottle whose upward body axis is +Z, positive world-Y pitch tilts that upward axis toward +X; negative pitch tilts it toward -X. A downward finger vector changes oppositely because it starts at -Z. This is a generic rotation example, not a target angle. Use CURRENT bottle-long-axis versus wooden-cradle geometry and actual examples to choose positive, negative or hold for pitch. Ignore XYZ distance.
align_source_above_receiver.rz: Positive world-Z yaw rotates a horizontal +X direction toward +Y, and +Y toward -X. It does not tilt a perfectly vertical bottle. Use current bottle orientation versus the inclined wooden channel to choose positive, negative or hold for yaw; do not copy the rotation sign of a different starting posture.

lower_to_place.z: Which world-Z motion brings the HELD BOTTLE into a suitable supported relationship with the rack? Selected rack support minus bottle surface Z={receiver_z_mm} mm. Positive is up, negative down. Account for visible body thickness: these are observed skin features, not centres or a contact certificate. Hold when a release attempt is visually reasonable.
lower_to_place.transition: Judge whether the visible bottle occupies the intended rack support arrangement sufficiently well for a release attempt. Use CURRENT main and side views and the archived AFTER relation. Continue for visibly needed seating correction. Advance when a release attempt is visually reasonable; nominal skin-point residuals need not be exactly zero. A projected overlap alone is insufficient, but hidden contact or already-proven post-release stability cannot be required before releasing. Restart for clearly lost bottle or wrong support region.

release.gripper: Open the fingers to release the manipulated object or control. Last executed gripper command={gripper_command}. Retain open once opening has actually executed.
release.transition: Release has executed {stage_steps} physical steps; the last actually executed gripper command is {gripper_command}. If this stage has zero physical steps, continue so the OPEN command can execute. After a real opening attempt has executed and the last command is open, ADVANCE to inspection. Do not require already-proven object support or activation before entering the stage that inspects it. An opening command alone is not task success.

inspect.x: The gripper has been opened. Keep world X unchanged while retracting the empty hand unless current RGB clearly requires lateral clearance; do not move the manipulated object.
inspect.y: The gripper has been opened. Keep world Y unchanged while retracting the empty hand unless current RGB clearly requires lateral clearance; do not move the manipulated object.
inspect.z: Expose the result by moving the OPEN empty hand away from the manipulated object. Positive world Z is UP. Choose positive while the hand still hides or crowds the control/placed bottle; a roughly 50mm measured upward retreat in stage_own_motion is normally enough to inspect. Hold once the view is clear. If the object still follows the hand, it has not visibly been released; do not claim support.
inspect.transition: First expose the manipulated object after opening: use CURRENT/PREVIOUS RGB and measured own retreat, not a hidden contact or success flag. If the bottle visibly fails to remain on its wooden cradle or the knob clearly remains unchanged, restart. After a clear view has actually been inspected, advance to end this visual inspection attempt. Reportable activation/support may remain uncertain; ending inspection is NOT a native-success certificate. Do not repeat an unchanged observation indefinitely.

stage_decision_rules.align_above_source: Advance ONLY if X and Y decisions are BOTH hold, the source reference is known, and the hand clearance is at least 80 mm. Otherwise continue coarse approach. Do not substitute an intended future alignment for these current facts.
stage_decision_rules.descend_to_source: If visual recovery is requested, restart. Otherwise continue if ANY listed X/Y/Z/rx/ry/rz decision is positive or negative. If ALL SIX are hold and the source reference is known, advance to an uncertain closure attempt; proven contact is not required. With unknown reference and all channels hold, follow the visual transition recommendation without treating unknown geometry as zero.
stage_decision_rules.close: If visual recovery is requested, restart. Otherwise continue when zero physical steps have executed in this phase or the last executed gripper command is not close. After a close command has actually executed in this phase, advance to its lift/turn test; contact proof is not required before the test.
stage_decision_rules.release: Continue when zero physical steps have executed in this phase or the last executed gripper command is not open. After an opening command has actually executed in this phase, advance to inspection. Do not demand proven support or activation before inspecting the result.

visual_stage_rules.lift: First allow a real upward lift test after closure. Advance when CURRENT main and side views show the bottle following the hand clear of the table with room to begin reorientation and approach. The bottle need not already have its final rack posture. Continue if a first lift test or more table separation is visibly needed. Restart if it clearly stays on the table or has dropped.
visual_stage_rules.align_source_above_receiver: Judge the physical bottle and receiving bay in CURRENT fixed views against the archived AFTER relationship. Advance when the held bottle is sufficiently lengthwise and above the selected bay to begin seating. Continue for a visibly needed approach or orientation correction. Nominal point-to-point bands and line directions guide motion; requiring all six corrections to be hold is not this exit. Do not substitute gripper location for bottle location. Restart for a clearly lost bottle or wrong bay; occlusion alone is not proof of loss.
visual_stage_rules.lower_to_place: Judge whether the visible bottle occupies the intended rack support arrangement sufficiently well for a release attempt. Use CURRENT main and side views and the archived AFTER relation. Continue for visibly needed seating correction. Advance when a release attempt is visually reasonable; nominal skin-point residuals need not be exactly zero. A projected overlap alone is insufficient, but hidden contact or already-proven post-release stability cannot be required before releasing. Restart for clearly lost bottle or wrong support region.
visual_stage_rules.inspect: After actual opening, inspect the CURRENT bottle, rack and empty hand. Continue until the hand is visibly separated and clear. Advance only when the bottle remains in the intended support arrangement across CURRENT and supplied PREVIOUS observations separated by an actually executed command. If there is no prior inspection interval yet, continue to expose and compare the outcome. Restart if it visibly falls off or remains attached to the hand. This visual classification is not a native success flag.
